output.summary: KEP-3619 proposes a new SupplementalGroupsPolicy API field so users can control which supplemental groups (including those from /etc/group in the image) are attached to the first container process, instead of changing the existing default behavior. The KEP is recorded as implemented and stable.
output.rationale: Container runtimes (containerd, CRI-O) merge groups from the image's /etc/group into the first process, which is not OCI-compliant and lets image authors bypass supplemental group policy. Maintainers rejected a cluster-wide feature gate and a breaking default change, so the KEP adds an opt-in per-pod field plus detection guidance. The sources show the design discussion and approval; they do not show the implementation rollout details beyond the status history.

alternatives.option: Fix the container runtimes (containerd, CRI-O) to match the OCI spec
alternatives.why_not: Thockin noted it would be a breaking change: "Changing the behavior would be a breaking change, same as we are debating here, so I would expect that it would be rejected."

alternatives.option: Cluster-wide feature gate (e.g. OCICompatibleSupplementalGroups) to change the default
alternatives.why_not: Thockin said "Feature gates are bounded-lifetime. They have to go away. At that point it's just a breaking change."

alternatives.option: Runtime-level configuration toggled per cluster, as proposed by mrunal patel
alternatives.why_not: Thockin called it "very fragile"; the source also notes it is not portable across k8s distros.

alternatives.option: Users modify their images to control supplemental groups
alternatives.why_not: The KEP alternatives note the con is that it is more work and users won't always have an option to do that.

evidence.quote: this KEP proposes a new API field named `SupplementalGroupsPolicy` that enables users to control supplemental groups attached to the first container process
To mitigate this, the cluster administrators will need to deploy a custom low-level container runtime
Feature gates are bounded-lifetime. They have to go away. At that point it's just a breaking change.
